content:
Dear Quillstone Payments Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. I bring six years of experience in analytics and data science, including more than four years as a data scientist, building machine-learning models and practical data workflows used by operational and growth teams. Quillstone’s focus on helping merchants get quick, low-friction support particularly interests me, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my applied modelling and production-data experience to that work.

At Thistlebox, I developed a weekly LightGBM demand-forecasting model for orders by recipe and region, forecasting up to six weeks ahead. Feature engineering for calendar, price and menu-position factors helped reduce WAPE from 23% to 14%, with an estimated 9% reduction in food waste. I implemented a scheduled workflow in Vertex AI Workbench that writes forecasts to BigQuery for operational use in Looker. I also built an XGBoost churn model scored weekly in BigQuery to target retention offers; a 10% holdout validation found churn decreased by 2.1 percentage points in the treated group.

Alongside modelling, I design and analyse around 40 A/B tests each year and built a Python and Streamlit sequential-testing calculator with Docker, now used by around 25 colleagues. The data platform team handles its deployment on Cloud Run. I also write production SQL in BigQuery and maintain dbt models. These experiences have taught me to connect model development with the workflows and decisions that make it useful, while working across teams and communicating results to leadership.

I hold an MSc in Statistics with distinction and bring a strong foundation in Python, statistical modelling and feature engineering, as well as hands-on experience with GCP data workflows. I would be glad to discuss how this background could support Quillstone’s work on AI systems for customer operations and merchant support. Thank you for your consideration.

Yours sincerely,
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, professional, and well structured. It uses specific evidence rather than generic claims, including WAPE improvement, food-waste reduction, churn impact, experiment volume, and user adoption. The progression from forecasting and churn modelling to experimentation and production data workflows is logical. It is also appropriately transparent that the data platform team handles deployment. The main content limitation is not writing quality but that the letter presents a strong data-science profile for a role requiring broader machine-learning engineering and customer-support AI experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is ATS-friendly: it uses standard paragraphs, no tables or graphics, a clear greeting, and the target job title appears in the opening paragraph. It includes supported keywords such as Python, machine learning, feature engineering, GCP, Vertex AI Workbench, BigQuery, Docker, Cloud Run, dbt, SQL, and A/B testing. However, it does not contain several exact job-ad terms, including chat assistants, RAG, model serving, monitoring, data versioning, MLOps, and orchestration tools such as MLflow, Kubeflow, or Airflow. These are genuine experience gaps according to the candidate information, so they should not be added merely for ATS purposes. AI-screening probability is moderate: the letter should pass basic keyword screening for Python, GCP, feature engineering, and production data workflows, but it is unlikely to rank as a close match for the specialised customer-support AI and MLOps requirements.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with the role's applied modelling, production data workflow, cloud, Python, feature engineering, experimentation, and operational decision-making aspects. The strongest evidence is the scheduled Vertex AI Workbench workflow writing outputs to BigQuery, the operational use of forecasts in Looker, and the weekly churn scoring workflow. The candidate's MSc Statistics and BSc Mathematics provide relevant quantitative preparation, but the ad specifically requests machine learning, computer science, or a related engineering degree. The candidate has more than four years as a data scientist, but the material does not establish four years as a machine learning engineer. The candidate also lacks documented experience with chat assistants or RAG, large text datasets, language-model fine-tuning, model monitoring, data versioning, named MLOps/orchestration platforms, and explicit model serving. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than defects that can be fixed through rewriting. The letter is strongest when positioning the candidate as an applied data scientist moving toward machine learning engineering, not as an already-qualified customer-support AI engineer.
critique.improvement_instructions:
Minor enhancement — In the opening paragraph, replace the general sentence beginning "I bring six years of experience" with a more role-specific but truthful version such as: "I bring six years of experience in analytics and data science, including more than four years developing and operationalising Python machine-learning models and scheduled GCP data workflows used by business teams." This makes the closest match to the role more visible while avoiding an unsupported claim of four years as a machine learning engineer.

Minor enhancement — In the final paragraph, change "hands-on experience with GCP data workflows" to "hands-on experience with Google Cloud Platform data workflows, including scheduled Vertex AI Workbench jobs, BigQuery scoring and production SQL, and dbt analytics models." This uses the job ad's cloud terminology and makes the concrete evidence easier for a recruiter or ATS to identify.

Minor enhancement — In the third paragraph, change "These experiences have taught me to connect model development with the workflows and decisions that make it useful" to "These experiences have taught me to connect model development with scheduled data workflows, operational reporting, experimentation decisions and cross-team adoption." This is more specific and better reflects the documented use of the candidate's work.

Dear Quillstone Payments Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. I bring six years of experience in analytics and data science, including more than four years developing and operationalising Python machine-learning models and scheduled GCP data workflows used by business teams. Quillstone’s focus on helping merchants get quick, low-friction support particularly interests me, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my applied modelling and production-data experience to that work.

At Thistlebox, I developed a weekly LightGBM demand-forecasting model for orders by recipe and region, forecasting up to six weeks ahead. Feature engineering for calendar, price and menu-position factors helped reduce WAPE from 23% to 14%, with an estimated 9% reduction in food waste. I implemented a scheduled workflow in Vertex AI Workbench that writes forecasts to BigQuery for operational use in Looker. I also built an XGBoost churn model scored weekly in BigQuery to target retention offers; a 10% holdout validation found churn decreased by 2.1 percentage points in the treated group.

Alongside modelling, I design and analyse around 40 A/B tests each year and built a Python and Streamlit sequential-testing calculator with Docker, now used by around 25 colleagues. The data platform team handles its deployment on Cloud Run. I also write production SQL in BigQuery and maintain dbt models. These experiences have taught me to connect model development with scheduled data workflows, operational reporting, experimentation decisions and cross-team adoption, while working across teams and communicating results to leadership.

I hold an MSc in Statistics with distinction and bring a strong foundation in Python, statistical modelling and feature engineering, as well as hands-on experience with Google Cloud Platform data workflows, including scheduled Vertex AI Workbench jobs, BigQuery scoring and production SQL, and dbt analytics models. I would be glad to discuss how this background could support Quillstone’s work on AI systems for customer operations and merchant support. Thank you for your consideration.

Yours sincerely,
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, professional and well structured. It uses specific metrics effectively, including the WAPE reduction, estimated food-waste reduction, churn improvement, experiment volume and user adoption of the calculator. The examples are credible and consistent with the Original Candidate Information. The main content limitation is that the letter presents strong applied data-science experience but does not establish direct experience with customer-support AI, language models or the full production software-engineering scope requested for this role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-readable: it uses standard headings-free paragraphs, conventional punctuation and relevant terms such as Python, machine learning, GCP, Vertex AI Workbench, BigQuery, Cloud Run, Docker, dbt, feature engineering and production SQL. However, AI screening probability is moderate-to-low for this specific vacancy because the letter does not contain supported evidence for several high-priority requirements, including chat assistants or RAG, model monitoring, data versioning, CI/CD, automated testing, text-data preparation and named MLOps tools. These are candidate gaps rather than defects that can be solved by adding unsupported keywords. The letter could also use the exact phrase “feature engineering” more prominently in the opening or closing alignment statement, although it already appears in the body.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is with Python modelling, feature engineering, forecasting, experimentation, GCP, scheduled data workflows, BigQuery, dbt and operational use of model outputs. The candidate also demonstrates practical collaboration and communication through work with operations, growth, product teams and leadership. The application is weaker against the role’s core customer-support AI requirements: the candidate material does not show chat assistants, retrieval-augmented generation, language-model fine-tuning, text-dataset preparation, four years specifically as a machine learning engineer, model monitoring, data versioning or the named MLOps/orchestration tools. The MSc Statistics and BSc Mathematics are quantitative degrees, but the material does not show a degree in machine learning, computer science or an engineering field. The letter should therefore position the candidate accurately as an applied data scientist transitioning toward machine learning engineering, while making the transferable production-workflow experience more explicit.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL: In the opening paragraph, replace the broad phrase “I bring six years of experience in analytics and data science, including more than four years developing and operationalising Python machine-learning models and scheduled GCP data workflows” with a more precise statement grounded in the evidence, such as: “I bring six years of experience in analytics and data science, including more than four years as a data scientist developing Python machine-learning models and scheduled Google Cloud workflows used by operations and growth teams.” This avoids sounding as though the candidate has four years specifically in a machine learning engineer title while preserving the strongest relevant evidence.

CRITICAL: In the second paragraph, explicitly identify the production workflow boundary when describing the forecasting system. Change “I implemented a scheduled workflow in Vertex AI Workbench” to “I implemented a scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook workflow that writes model outputs to BigQuery for operational use in Looker.” This uses the candidate’s exact portfolio evidence and makes the deployment pattern more concrete without implying unsupported ownership of model serving or platform operations.

CRITICAL: In the third paragraph, make the software-engineering contribution precise. Change “built a Python and Streamlit sequential-testing calculator with Docker, now used by around 25 colleagues” to “built and containerised a Python and Streamlit sequential-testing calculator, writing the Dockerfile; the data platform team manages its deployment on Cloud Run, and the tool is used by around 25 colleagues.” This accurately highlights Docker and Cloud Run while clearly separating the candidate’s work from the platform team’s deployment responsibility.

MINOR: In the final paragraph, add one sentence that connects the demonstrated experience to the target domain without claiming customer-support AI experience. For example: “I would bring the same approach of turning operational data into reliable, actionable outputs to merchant-support problems such as prioritisation, routing and agent decision support.” Place this before “I would be glad to discuss...” so the motivation is more specific to the advertised team.

MINOR: In the final paragraph, replace “hands-on experience with Google Cloud Platform data workflows, including scheduled Vertex AI Workbench jobs, BigQuery scoring and production SQL, and dbt analytics models” with “hands-on experience with Google Cloud Platform, including scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook jobs, weekly BigQuery model scoring, production SQL and dbt analytics models.” This improves ATS matching for “Google Cloud Platform,” “BigQuery,” “production SQL” and “dbt” while remaining faithful to the candidate information.
